Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a first-draft MAP (BRH-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short note on lead-time assumptions. High-level summary below; full timeline in the MAP attachment.

Proposed MAP highlights:
- Evaluation sprint (2 weeks): initial integration + smoke tests, run with Redwood Hosted and a short Dedicated proof-of-performance (PoP) cluster.
- Acceptance gate A (integration): infra sign-off on networking, auth, and prefix-caching behavior. 3 business days to validate.
- Evaluation sprint 2 (canary): 1 week canary on Dedicated (pinned instance), 50 QPS target for canary. Acceptance gate B: performance & cost signal. 5 business days.
- Production tranche (staged rollout): initial tranche (200 QPS equivalent) staged over 2 weeks; final acceptance: SLA baseline validated.

Lead-time guidance (typical):
- Dedicated (hosted dedicated pool): provisioning lead time 6–8 weeks from PO/commit for initial tranche; subsequent tranches ~2–3 weeks if within planned capacity.
- Private (VPC + on-prem option): VPC private deployment in partner cloud: 8–10 weeks; on-prem (air-gapped) 12–16 weeks depending on rack/host procurement and local compliance.

Rough GPU sizing (initial guidance):
- Canary stage: 4 x A100 80GB equiv (or 8 x A10‑class) in a balanced pool to support 50 QPS with KV cache warmed for small models.
- Initial prod tranche (200 QPS, KV heavy): 20–24 x A100 80GB equiv (or 40 x A10) depending on model family and sequence-length.
- We recommend reserving ~20% headroom for burst and autoscale buffer.

Next steps I suggest: review the attached MAP and mark acceptance windows. If procurement needs a pedantically granular lead-time table for PO, I’ll pull that from Ops.

Mina Haddad
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Hey Samantha — quick technical clarifications to help tune sizing numbers.

On Thu, Apr 20, 2027 at 11:02 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Mina —
> 
> Appreciate the clear asks. I attached a first-draft MAP ...

Concrete sizing assumptions I used for the MAP:
- Model family: mix of 7B dense + 13B instruction-tuned models for prod. If you adopt exclusively 13B small models, you can reduce A100-equivalent count by ~25%.
- Sequence length assumption: 256 tokens average; 1024 token worst-case for batch planning.
- KV-cache hit target for production: 65–75% (we recommend a warmup window and a prefix-caching policy).

Suggested Dedicated pool config for first tranche (example):
- 6 pods x 4 x A10080 GPU allocation per pod (24 total GPUs) — tuned for throughput and KV cache locality.
- Autoscale policy: +2 pods (8 GPUs) with 5-minute cooldown for burst.

On Private/on-prem: allow an extra 2–3 weeks for hardware procurement and 1 week for Redwood on-site validation (if required). For VPC deployments in public cloud region, we can often do 6–8 week turnaround if partner capacity booked ahead.

Happy to sketch an alternative lower-cost config if procurement is tight (mixed-quant 8-bit kernels + more aggressive batching).

— Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Samantha / procurement team —

Good news: we can tighten the windows if BlueRidge is willing to sign a 12-month tranche commitment for the initial pool. Below is the PO-ready summary and the acceptance metric table you can paste into your PR/PO. I also attached BRH-MAP-v1.xlsx with updated min/max lead times per deployment.

PO summary (one-paragraph):
Redwood Inference will provision an initial Dedicated GPU pool for BlueRidge Health to support an initial production tranche (target 200 QPS equivalent). Lead-time windows depend on deployment mode: Dedicated hosted pool: 6–8 weeks (min 6, max 8) from confirmed PO and signed contract; VPC private deployment: 8–10 weeks (min 8, max 10) from PO and network prep; On-prem air-gapped: 12–16 weeks (min 12, max 16) from PO and hardware delivery. This PO assumes a 12-month reserved commitment for the initial tranche; changes to tranche sizing or term may extend lead times.

Acceptance metrics (for MAP acceptance gate B/production tranche):
- Latency: p95 tail <= 420 ms for 95% of test runs (synthetic baseline, 256-token avg).
- Error rate: request error-rate <= 0.3% measured over 24h rolling window.
- Throughput: sustained throughput >= 90% of 200 QPS target for a 2-hour continuous run with KV cache warmed.
- Quality regression: automated evals on the provided prompt set must show no >1.5% drop in top-line pass rate against the baseline.

Next operational steps:
1) Procurement: confirm PO window and attach the PO summary above to the PR.
2) BlueRidge infra: mark acceptance windows in the MAP workbook and confirm the integration validation owners.
3) Redwood Ops: we will hold a hardware reservation window once PO is cleared (we recommend reserving capacity immediately to hit the 6-week lower bound).

If that all looks good I propose a short 30-minute alignment call early next week to lock the PO text and the dates. Please suggest times.

Thanks —
